text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall-n7: smart-routing alert - multiple region fallback + cache reuse detected (high error rate). See summary below.

maria: got the page, joining. what's the impact?

oncall-n7: I'm on it. what's the metric spike?

incident-bot: Alerts: 5xx rate on /v1/generate up from 0.02% to 3.7% in last 6m. Latency SLO breaches reporting in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Fallback loop observed where requests keep bouncing between region fallback and model-variant fallback. KV cache hits with mismatched model_id found in traces.

sam: quick summary from infra: a recent routing policy change (policy id rp-2026-03-12) relaxed compatibility checks for model variants to allow higher throughput. It inadvertently allowed selection of v2-small variants for requests pinned to v3-large; the routing decision layer then keys KV cache by region+model_name only, not variant, so we hit cached KV entries from v2 for v3 requests => wrong KV prefix, leading to malformed past-key reuse and token corruption.

jordan: oh wow. so incorrect prefixing + relaxed compatibility = wrong cached kv being reused. any customer reports?

beth-cs: support reports: 9 customers reported garbled completions, 2 flagged as "safety/regression" (one enterprise transcript with PII leakage). Raised to priority-high. Customer A (enterprise) paused traffic.

oncall-n7: ok immediate mitigation checklist: 1) disable rp-2026-03-12 rollout 2) set routing policy to strict compatibility 3) invalidate KV cache keys for affected region/model prefixes 4) roll forward a hotfix to make cache key include exact variant id.

maria: I'm pushing a temporary kill-switch to routing: `/admin/routing/set_policy?policy_id=rp-2026-02-stable` — will revert to previous. executing now.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: routing-policy-revert @maria requested. CI passed. Starting: deploy-1834.

sam: while that's rolling, we should flush wrong KV entries to stop reused state. I have a script to list keys and delete by prefix.

sam: command (careful):
```
# list keys in us-east-1 for model "redwood-v3" but without variant
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  "https://kv-admin.internal/list?prefix=us-east-1:redwood-v3" | jq -r '.keys[]'

# delete keys found
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  "https://kv-admin.internal/delete_prefix" -d '{"prefix":"us-east-1:redwood-v3"}'
```

lee: executing listing now. will snapshot keys before deletion and upload to /incidents/1772504321/artifacts.

lee: listing done. ~48k keys. snapshot uploaded: https://internal.storage/snapshots/1772504321-keys.tar.gz

lee: starting delete of affected prefixes in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. monitoring for regressions.

maria: routing revert completed (deploy-1834 finished). policy now: rp-2026-02-stable. rolling restarts of routing agents in us-east-1 started.

oncall-n7: nice. kv purge in progress?

lee: purge finished for redwood-v3 base prefixes. I left variant-specific prefixes untouched. Post-purge error rate dropping from 3.7% -> 0.6% in 7m.

jordan: partial mitigation success. we still see some degraded responses — likely due to cached serving instances with in-memory kv state. need to rotate pods that hold warm KV caches.

oncall-n7: initiating rolling restart of inference pods with draining. command: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-us-east-1 --namespace=prod --selector=role=inference`

maria: started. ETA ~12m for full rotation.

beth-cs: customers notified: sent update to affected tenancies - ETA for full resolution 20-30m. escalation to account teams underway.

sam: one more fix: change cache key generation to include exact `variant_id` (e.g., redwood-v3|variant:v3.large|region:us-east-1) — I'll prep a patch, but that's postmortem work. For now we must ensure no further policy rollouts push rp-2026-03-12.

oncall-n7: agreed. locking rollout pipeline for routing policies. notifying product.

deploy-bot: rollback: routing-policy-revert (deploy-1834) -> succeeded.

lee: after restarts, error rate down to 0.07%. 2 customers still showing funky completions — investigating traces.

jordan: quick forensic note: trace id 1a2b3c shows a request that was routed to us-east-1:v2-small however model_name header was redwood-v3 and kv prefix collision matched v2 cache entry. The serving layer didn't validate variant-level kv signature. we'll add that validation.

maria: adding incident tag and channel: #incidents/1772504321, creating incident ticket in PagerDuty > Jira: IN-2026-042. assigning postmortem to sam.

sam: I'll own the postmortem. immediate action items:
- [ ] patch routing to require variant compatibility check (hotfix planned)
- [ ] change kv cache key to include variant_id (PR in review)
- [ ] add variant signature validation in serving runtime (follow-up)
- [ ] customer outreach: Beth to lead
- [ ] retention of key snapshot & logs (lee)

beth-cs: customer messages queued, legal alerted for PII flag, CS is ready to run remediation calls.

oncall-n7: handing off to day oncall @maria in 15m. I'll stay available for 30m.

maria: thanks. I'll follow up with status updates in 30m and postmortem in 48h.

incident-bot: Incident IN-2026-042 created. Severity: sev-2. Notifying execs.

sam: PR for cache-key change opened: https://phabricator.internal/D12345 — reviewers @maria @lee. This will prevent future reuse even if routing policies are loose.

lee: uploaded extra traces and the key snapshot to artifacts. link: https://internal.storage/incidents/1772504321/

beth-cs: final customer update sent. most customers resumed normal traffic; one enterprise awaiting remediation call.

jordan: post-incident immediate retrospective: we must add automated unit tests that assert cache key uniqueness across variant changes and add a canary runway for routing policy changes.

maria: agreed. adding to IN-2026-042 action list. closing slack thread when postmortem posted.

oncall-n7: thanks team. leaving channel. :white_check_mark:
